sentences.text:
Applicant has filed this first bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 in connection with Crime No. 383/2022 registered at P.S - Pipliyamandi, District- Mandsaur (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 34(2) of M.P. Excise Act and sections 420, 467, 468. 471 of IPC.
As per prosecution story, n 19.12.2022, Police received secret information, that in a white color truck bearing registration number RJ- 02-GA-2635 is going to carry illicit liquor.
On that information police reached the spot and stopped the alleged vehicle and searching the same police found 8623 Bulk liter of liquor from the possession of accused persons.
After that, memo u/s 27 of Evidence Act has been recorded of the co-accused persons and they disclosed the name of the present applicant.

Thereafter, the police registered case under sections 34 (2) of MP. Excise Ac and sections Hanumanram vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26855891/
1 420,467,468,471 of the IPC against the applicant and other co- ccused persons.
Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: There is no legal evidence available on record to connect the applicant with the aforementioned offence.
He was not present on the spot at the time of the incident.
He has falsely been implicated in the instant case on the basis of memo given by co-accused under section 27 of the Evidence Act, but nothing has been recovered from his possession.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the applicant is required..
Applicant is in custody since 27/12/2022.
He is permanent resident of District- Mulani Badner ( Rajasthan).
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

Per-contra, learned PL for respondent - State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection,
but fairly admits that no criminal antecednet has been found against the applicant.
Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.

Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that the applicant has falsely been implicated in the instant case on the basis of memo given by co-accused under section 27 of the Evidence Act, but nothing has been recovered from his possession; he was not present on the spot at the time of the incident.

he is in custody since 27/12/2022; investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed,
therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the applicant is required and possibility of delay in conclusion of the trial cannot be ruled out, in view of the evidence available on record, I deem it proper to release the accused / applicant on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs. 1,00,000/-
(Rs. One Lac only) with two sureties ( out of which, one local surety) in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C., Certified copy, as per Rules.
